items.title: Sid Davilla Interview, 1969-04-17
items.q: when I first, Leon Prem, I think opened his club shortly after the war, and he was the first one to put a taste of Dixieland on the street.

ctx.x: No, no, it was at the 500 Club. Oh, this was at the 500 Club. This was before you opened your place.

About 47, 1948. So actually, that was the first, now that I know of, that was the first little Dixieland music in this area, in the French Quarter. Because prior to that, before I went to the Army in 42, there were several clubs on the street, and one in particular was the, uh, ballet club. And I had a band in there for a couple of years. But we played for dancing, and we played for shows, but we didn't make any attempt at playing Dixieland music. We played the pop music of the day, you know, for dancing, and of…

Amazing. Can you remember that before, like in, uh, before the war, can you remember it at all? I mean, there was... Before the war. Or, say, around early, very early 40s, there really wasn't any, any jazz.
